title: Percent-encoded passwords in connection URIs: the span is the encoded text as written
summary: Connection URIs for MongoDB, MySQL and an AMQP broker whose password contains reserved characters written as percent-encoded triplets (%40, %3A, %2F, %23, %25, %5B, %5D) in the user-info position. Synthetic passwords on reserved example hosts.
rationale: The password as it sits in the text is the percent-encoded form, not the decoded value. Public grammar documentation tells authors to encode reserved characters, so the secret span runs from the first colon of the user-info to the at-sign before the host and includes every percent triplet. Stopping at the first percent sign, or covering only the decoded characters, leaves secret bytes in place. The decoded value is a separate (derived) representation: its relation to the original span is the lineage question of #94/#95 and is not asserted here. Host, database, vhost and user are public parts.

expectation.rationale: The grammar facts are documented by the database and broker vendors: the password is the text after the user name in user-info, and reserved characters appear percent-encoded inside it. That the project expects such a password to be reported, with the range covering the whole encoded run, is a project policy decision (the same position already held for the family: only the password bytes are secret, a wider range is acceptable). Needs a recorded maintainer decision and a non-author reviewer before it can leave draft.

sources.supports: If the username or password includes the characters $ : / ? # [ ] @, those characters must be converted using percent encoding; the page shows a password written D1fficultP%40ssw0rd in the user-info of mongodb:// and mongodb+srv:// strings.
sources.locator: sections "Find Your Self-Hosted Deployment's Connection String" and "Additional Connection String Examples"

sources.supports: Percent encoding must be used for reserved characters in the elements of the URI-like string; the syntax is [scheme://][user[:[password]]@]host[:port][/schema][?attributes].
sources.locator: URI-like connection string syntax and the percent-encoding paragraph

sources.supports: The amqp userinfo is username [ ":" password ] with password = *( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims ); percent-encoded octets in the username and password are decoded before the SASL exchange and regarded as UTF-8.
sources.locator: sections "The amqp URI scheme" and "Username and password"

sources.supports: Percent-encoded octet is a percent sign followed by two hexadecimal digits; gen-delims are : / ? # [ ] @.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Issue #111 (parent #92). Span convention for every fixture of this case: the secret is the password exactly as written, from the character after the first colon of the user-info to the character before the at-sign that precedes the host, percent triplets included. Related reviews: generic:connection-string-password basis review (#52, owner of evidence-class restoration for the existing family fixtures), sibling grammar and benign cases under the same family in records/cases. Encoded-representation and reconstruction links: #94 and #95 (parent #92). Downstream handoff: credential-eval (execution, decoded finding to source-range mapping), redact-secret (decoding and action policy), redact-secret-benchmarks (qualification and actual-output regression); none of those policies is changed here.
